A central processing unit ( CPU ), also known as a central processor , main processor , or simply processor , is the primary processor in a given computer . [ 1 ] [ 2 ] Its electronic circuitry executes instructions of a computer program , such as arithmetic , logic, controlling, and input/output (I/O) operations. [ 3 ] [ 4 ] [ 5 ] This role contrasts with that of external components, such as main memory and I/O circuitry, [ 6 ] and specialized coprocessors such as graphics processing units (GPUs).
